newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Texaco-led group said to clinch Philippine deal.
newsitem.headline: Texaco-led group said to clinch Philippine deal.

text.p: The Philippines National Power Corp (Napocor) said on Friday it would probably award a 304-megawatt power sales contract to San Pascual Cogeneration Co (SPCC) as no other company had submitted a competitive bid.
"Most likely the contract will go to San Pascual since there were no competitive proposals submitted at bidding yesterday (Thursday)," said Cerael Donggay, Napocor negotiating committee chairman.
SPCC, a consortium comprising Texaco Inc, Caltex (Philippines) Inc and Mission Energy of the United States, has submitted an unsolicited proposal to build a 304-MW plant in Batangas, south of Manila.
Under the law, Napocor has to allow other interested companies to match an unsolicited proposal.
Donggay said the final round of negotiations for the contract with San Pascual should start soon and be awarded within the first quarter.
Last year four foreign companies, Itochu Corp, Nissho Iwai, Salcon Power Corp of Singapore and California Energy of the United States, bought bidding documents for the project.
The power plant, which will require investment estimated at $400 million, is scheduled for commercial operation by 2001.
